findings.issue: Uncontrolled inputs synced via refs and two effects, including a pre-hydration catch-up, duplicate home-grown state-management logic that React Router's useSearchParams would give directly
findings.suggestion: Make q/type/generation controlled inputs driven by useSearchParams (updating on debounce); delete the ref-sync and catch-up effects

findings.issue: Team cookie is read-modify-write per action with no concurrency guard; two rapid submissions are last-write-wins
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for this feature; if it ever matters, version the cookie or serialize updates client-side via fetcher.state

findings.issue: Errors are only logged in DEV, so production loader/action failures are invisible
findings.suggestion: Log the error server-side (or rethrow to the framework logger) before rendering the generic message

findings.issue: Cache retains expired entries until they are next requested; fine here because keys are bounded by the API snapshot, but worth stating
findings.suggestion: Optionally delete the entry in a finally when expired, or note the bound in the comment

findings.issue: Catch-all route's component returns null; the rendered 404 UI actually comes from the root ErrorBoundary, so the component is dead weight
findings.suggestion: Either render the NotFound UI here (with a route ErrorBoundary) or drop the component and keep only the throwing loader

findings.issue: versionGroupOrders fetches the version-group list plus every group record on each Pokémon page load (cached per URL for 60s)
findings.suggestion: Cache the assembled Map under a single key like getIndex does, so page loads don't depend on ~30 URL-cache entries being warm

summary: A well-executed, current-idiom React Router v8 framework app: typed route modules, loaders owning URL state, fetcher-based mutations with a server cookie, and a clean express production server. The only structural weakness is hand-rolled input synchronization around the filter and game controls where useSearchParams would be simpler. I'd merge it with nits.
